title: Strengthen OSCORE parity fixture tests (P3 review findings)
description: Five P3 findings from wave-1 codereview of the 6.8.9 parity work: (1) fixture pins only the protect direction — add a tamper-rejection vector (modified ciphertext/tag must fail to decrypt) derived from the EDHOC context. (2) Python drift-guard compares oracle to its own fixture (not an independent oracle) — chain anchors bottom out in Python; document or add an external anchor (e.g. RFC 8613 appendix vector). (3) rust context_parity.rs test truncates vector decoded_timestamp u64->u32 with as u32 — assert range first so fixture drift fails loudly. (4) generator + python test couple to private ctx._construct_nonce — a refactor breaks them; prefer a stable public path or pin with a comment. (5) generate_oscore_context_parity.py patches os.urandom but secrets.token_bytes binds os.urandom at import — harmless today (echo_recovery not in fixture) but any future field derived via secrets makes regeneration silently nondeterministic; patch secrets.token_bytes too.
